text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS
- Hungary has completed the transition to market economy, the Prime Minister's Office said in a report.
- Christian Democrat Party President Gyorgy Giczy said he will initiate the dissolution of party's parliamentary group.
- Free Democrat President Gabor Kuncze rejected party ideologist Miklos Tamas Gaspar's proposal that the party quit the coalition.
- The Polish, Czech and Hungarian foreign ministers met in Prague to discuss accession strategies.
- Foreign Minister Laszlo Kovacs will meet his Slovak counterpart today in Komarno.
- The nationalist mayor of the Romanian town of Cluj said he will not meet Hungary's newly appointed consul to Cluj.
- The country's current account balance closed May with a record surplus of $148 million.
- Imports rose 13.8 percent in the first five months of the year.
- The Agriculture Ministry expects agriculutral exports of some $3 billion this year.
- Gyorgy Suranyi, President of the National Bank of Hungary could be a candidate for the presidency of the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development.
- Budapest Stock Excahnge CEO Jozsef Rotyis will step down as of September 1.
- The supervisory board of privatisation agency APV Rt said it disapproves the Postabank-APV asset swap.
- Ikarus has received an $43 million export financing loan.
VILAGGAZDASAG
- U.S. research institute PlanEcon said the Hungarian Central Statistical Office's data are misleading while a domestic group said the central bank's domestic savings calculations need correction.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- The senior coalition partner Socialist Party leads in an opinion poll witha 32 percent popularity, followed by opposition Smallholders.
